column2: ENGLISH

The captain of the Erengrad Convoy comes up from the harbour with his officers behind him, salt-stained and grey-bearded, and kneels before [Root.GetTitledFirstName]. For years the Convoy sailed for whoever paid best. Now it will sail for Erengrad and for its lord. He swears on the Lynsk and on Manann's trident, and asks only that his ships be kept in good timber and his crews in good vodka.
Rise, Convoy Master.

The Convoy Master spreads the charts across the table. The warehouses are full and the ships are ready, he says, and every port in the north is hungry for something. Marienburg buys amber and furs. Salzenmund wants timber and silver. L'Anguille pays well for furs and silver, the jarls of Norsca for grain and silver. Sudenburg, far to the south, needs timber and grain, and the Elves of Ulthuan, furthest of all, will pay a fortune for furs and amber. Where shall the Convoy sail?
To Marienburg.
To Salzenmund.
To L'Anguille in Bretonnia.
To the halls of the Norscan jarls.
South to Sudenburg.
To Ulthuan itself.

The guild masters crowd the harbour office, each one shouting that his goods are the ones the Convoy must carry. Furs from the trappers of the oblast, timber from the forests of the Lynsk, silver from the mountains, amber washed up on the northern shore, and grain from the black earth of the steppe. The holds have room for one great cargo.
Furs.
Timber.
Silver.
Amber.
Grain.

Forty galleys of the Erengrad Convoy put out from the harbour with the whole city on the quays to see them go. The priests of the Temple of Manann stand ready to bless the ships for a donation. The Convoy Master must now take command of the fleet and bring it into the chosen port. If he has not done so within three years, the cargo will be lost.
Bless the ships at the Temple of Manann.
Sail, and trust to the Convoy Master.

Word comes by fast rider: the Erengrad Convoy has made port at Marienburg, the richest city in the Old World. The Wasteland merchants have come down to the docks to bargain, and the Convoy Master is selling the cargo and buying for the voyage home.

Word comes by fast rider: the Erengrad Convoy has made port at Salzenmund in Nordland. The Nordlanders have been waiting all season for ships from Kislev, and the Convoy Master has sold the cargo before it is even off the ships.

Word comes by fast rider: the Erengrad Convoy has made port in Bretonnia. The merchants of L'Anguille are haughty and slow to pay, but they do pay in the end, and the Convoy Master has made a good bargain.

Word comes by fast rider: the Erengrad Convoy has come safely into a Norscan harbour, and the jarl did not burn it. He has bought the cargo with silver taken from someone else, and he has asked that the Convoy come again next year.

Word comes by fast rider: the Erengrad Convoy has made it all the way south to Sudenburg, further than any Kislevite fleet has sailed in a generation. The cargo has sold at a price the guild masters will not believe.

Word comes by fast rider: the Erengrad Convoy has made port on the shores of Ulthuan. The Asur have looked at our ships with pity, but they have paid for the cargo in gold and gems, and the Convoy Master is already planning the next voyage.
Bring the Convoy home.

There is no word from the Convoy. Months pass and the guild masters stop asking. When at last the galleys straggle back into Erengrad, their holds are empty and the cargo is gone, rotted, sold for nothing or thrown overboard. The city is not pleased.
A bitter loss.
The Convoy has come home, and with it the share that [Root.GetTitledFirstName] bought in the voyage. Silver, and a good deal more of it than was paid in. The other boyars of the Duma are taking note.

The Convoy has come home, and the share that [Root.GetTitledFirstName] bought in the voyage has come to nothing. The cargo was ruined at sea, or sold too cheap, or stolen by the clerks. The guild masters shrug. That is trade.
So it goes on the sea.

The richest fur merchant in Erengrad has made his fortune and everyone knows it. Now he wants what money cannot buy: to be raised to the druzhina and seated in the Duma with the boyars. He has brought a chest of silver to show his gratitude in advance. The boyars of the city are watching closely.
Raise him. Silver is as good as blood.
A merchant is a merchant. Send him home.

A guild warehouse on the docks burned in the night with a season's furs inside it. The watch found boyars' men with torches in the next street, and every merchant in Erengrad knows who paid them. The guilds have come to [Root.GetTitledFirstName] demanding justice.
Punish the boyars who did this.
Pay the guild for its loss.
Let them settle it among themselves.
A guild clerk leaves a heavy purse on the table and backs away bowing. The guilds would be so very grateful, he says, if the harbour tax were a little lighter this year. Nobody else needs to know.
Take the purse.
Send it back. The tax stands.

An old boyar house of Erengrad, rich in ancestors and poor in everything else, wants to marry its daughter to the son of a guild master. The boyar asks [Root.GetTitledFirstName] to bless the match. The guildsman has already paid for the wedding.
Bless the match. Old blood and new silver.
Forbid it. The druzhina does not marry trade.
A casting went wrong in the Cannoneers' Compound. The mould cracked, the bronze ran wild and half the foundry is ash. The master cannoneer, his beard singed off, asks for gold to rebuild.
Pay for the repairs.
The cannoneers made the mess. Let them clean it up.

The Compound's guards have caught a man copying plans in the drawing-room at night. He says he is a merchant from Talabheim. His papers say he is a merchant from Talabheim. Everyone knows he is an agent of the Gunnery School of Nuln.
Hang him on the harbour wall.
Ransom him back to Nuln.
Let him go, with a false set of plans.

A Dwarf engineer from Karak Kadrin has come to the Compound. He looks at our guns, snorts, and says that for the right price he can make them shoot twice as far and burst half as often. He wants his price in gold, in advance.
Pay the Dwarf.
Our guns are good enough. Send him back to his mountain.

The Elven Quarter of Erengrad is one of the largest in the Old World, and its traders keep to themselves. Now they have sent word. A mage of the White Tower who has lived among them for a century asks to serve at [Root.GetTitledFirstName]'s court. And the traders offer a contract with the merchant houses of Ulthuan, for a price.
Welcome the mage to court.
Sign the Ulthuan contract.
Neither. Elves never give anything freely.

The foreign merchants of Erengrad are quarrelling again over the best wharf. The Empire's men say they were there first. The Bretonnians say they pay the most. The Tileans say nothing and bribe the harbourmaster. All three ask [Root.GetTitledFirstName] to decide.
Give it to the Empire's merchants.
Give it to the Bretonnians.
Give it to the Tileans.

Refugees from the north have been pouring into the Low City, the sprawl of tents and shacks beneath Erengrad's walls. They bring their hands for work, but also their hunger and their sickness. The city guard want to clear the tents before winter.
Let them stay. Erengrad needs hands.
Clear the tents and drive them off.

When Erengrad burned long ago, the Temple of Manann was the only building to survive. It was built like a ship and simply floated free on the harbour. Its priests ask [Root.GetTitledFirstName] for gold to keep their temple seaworthy, and promise Manann's favour on every ship that sails from Erengrad.
Give gold to the Sea God's temple.
Manann will have to wait.

The masons and carpenters have done their work. Erengrad rises again from the ashes with salvaged stone and Convoy timber, and the guild district comes back faster than anyone hoped. The people cheer [Root.GetTitledFirstName] in the streets.
Erengrad stands!
Convoy Master
The Convoy Master leads the Erengrad Convoy on its trade runs. The fleet will only find its way into a distant port with the Convoy Master in command.
Charter the Erengrad Convoy
Take the Erengrad Convoy into your service. Its captain will join your court as Convoy Master, and the fleet will sail for Erengrad from now on.
Send out the Erengrad Convoy

Choose a port and a cargo, and send the Convoy out to trade. You must put your Convoy Master in command of the fleet and sail it to the chosen port within three years. The right cargo for the market and a long voyage pay the most.
Call the Convoy to War
Call the Convoy's forty galleys to fight for you until the peace. Once in ten years.
Sponsor a Convoy Run
Buy a share in the next voyage of the Erengrad Convoy. The Duma will think better of you now, and most of the time the share will come back in two years with a profit.
Buy a Battery from the Cannoneers
Buy a battery of great guns from the Cannoneers' Compound of Erengrad. Your sieges will go faster.
Rebuild Erengrad
Erengrad lies sacked and burned. Pay for its rebuilding, and the guilds will come back.
Has a Convoy Master who is free to sail
The Convoy is not already at sea
Convoy Recently Sent
The Erengrad Convoy needs time to refit before it can sail again.
Convoy Recently Called
The Convoy's warships have been called to war, and the guilds will not lend them again soon.
Convoy Sponsor
This character has a share in a recent Convoy run.
Erengrad Battery
A battery of great guns from the Cannoneers' Compound of Erengrad.
Dwarf-Improved Battery
A battery of Erengrad guns, improved by a Dwarf engineer. They shoot further and burst less often.
Norscan Trade-Friendship
A Norscan jarl lets our ships pass and buys our goods.
White Star Escort
The Knights of the White Star escort this character's ships through the Sea of Claws.
Ship's Fever
This character caught a fever at sea.
Recent Voyage
This character had an adventure at sea recently.
Convoy Trade Boom
The Convoy's success has brought a flood of trade to the city.
Burned Warehouses
Warehouses on the docks have burned, and the trade suffers for it.
Crowded Low City
Refugees crowd the tents of the Low City. They work cheap and pay taxes, but they also bring sickness and unrest.
Favour of Manann
The Temple of Manann prays for the city and blesses every ship that sails from its harbour free of charge.
Ulthuan Contract
The merchant houses of Ulthuan trade through the city's Elven Quarter.
Sacked
The city was sacked when it fell. Its guilds have fled and its warehouses lie in ashes.
Rebuilt
The city has been rebuilt with new stone and new money.
Favoured the guilds
Slighted me
Favoured our merchants
Sponsored the Convoy
Elven Sea Chart

A chart of the seas of the world drawn by Asur navigators, with currents and coasts that no human captain has ever seen. The Convoy Master won it in a game of dice with an Elven sea captain, or so he says.
Engraved Swivel Gun
A small bronze swivel gun from the Cannoneers' Compound of Erengrad, engraved with runes by a Dwarf engineer. It is too pretty to fire, though it has been fired, often.
Leviathan's Tooth
A tooth as long as a man's arm, cut from the jaw of a sea monster of the Sea of Claws. Sailors touch it for luck.
